utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Pilipovic, you are standing. Is there any observation you would like to make?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Good morning. Before we start the cross-examination of the witness, I would like to inform the Chamber that yesterday, at 1800 hours, we received the fax from our learned colleagues by which they informed us, as I understand, that today we would be examining Witness H. However, we were not informed whether the witness who is supposed to come after Mensur Jusic, Witness M, will not be examined today. Could we be informed about the changes in the schedule? And also to inform us whether the witness who is supposed to come after is going to be examined or not. So I'm not sure whether we're supposed to get ready for Witness M after Mr. Jusic. Thank you, Your Honour. And also, I would also like to be informed by my learned colleagues whether we would be getting a schedule of the witnesses for next week. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please respond, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, so that we don't waste time - thank you - and also to allow the Prosecution to find out about what they have to tell us, I wanted to give you an answer about the question that you asked me. It's about the translations, the interpretation. Could I do it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. On page 31, 51 on the French transcript, a question asked by Mr. Mundis, I said, in French, and I'm now quoting in French: "I would have appreciated --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you allow me just to change to the French channel so that I can hear you. [Interpretation] Could you now hear me? Could you now please read in French. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I was doing, but I will do it again. So what I said in French was the following, and thank you for listening in French. I am now quoting: "I would have appreciated a question which would consist of finding out where the shooting was coming from rather than a question asking if the shooting was coming from that location," which appeared to be a leading question, i.e., a misleading question. Now, when I'm looking at the English interpretation of this passage - which is in my English transcript, non-definitive version, but I have it on my computer, and the hour was 13:45:35 - we can see that the translation simply doesn't have one part of what I said, so it's not complete. So the reason why I'm saying this, Mr. President, is that very often there are problems that happen, and it seems that the Chamber quotes me in an incorrect manner, which I was able to check in the French transcript, and I can perhaps check it on the audiotape so that there could be no misunderstanding between us which perhaps come from the interpretation. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let me just make one remark: A simultaneous translation is very difficult to perform and sometimes, because of the speed of speech and for many other reasons, might cause some imprecision in the translation at the moment. That's especially the reason why all the tapes are still there. I'm always open for any correction in that respect. I thank you for your assistance. What I would like most is that if there's any difficulty in -- any doubt as to whether the translation is perfect or less perfect, to indicate. If it's of vital importance at that moment, please immediately interfere. If it is of minor importance, please write it down. I would say make just a small note and provide it to the Chamber through the Registry so that we can give it to those who assist in working on these transcripts at night. So I would invite you to make a clear distinction between where it's a minor mistake and where it's really of importance for the hearing of the case at that moment. But I thank you. And you know that I am quite sensitive to whatever translation problems there are. Unfortunately, I've got only two languages I can understand. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The only letter that I'm aware of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you would have a possibility, because you did read to us in French the lines, those parts of your questions, I would invite you to provide us - I don't know whether you have it at hand at this moment also - but exactly what the English translation was so we also can make our assessment on how defective it would have been. We prefer, as a matter of fact, to have both languages then perhaps printed out so that we can compare it. And we really are interested to see what it is exactly. Now, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, last night the Defence was sent a letter from the Prosecution which consisted of one sentence. It read, "Please find attached a corrigendum to the schedule and corresponding exhibits of Witness H." Is that the letter to which my friend refers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is. Is that true? Yes, that's the letter --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am very sorry, but I was trying to track down the hard copies, you see, and I only heard a small part of his intervention. So I'm now going to plunge into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that the letter you are referring to is the letter consisting of just one line: "Please find attached a corrigendum to the schedule and corresponding exhibits of Witness H." That's the letter you -- it was Ms. Pilipovic, it was you who --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In fact, to be absolutely precise, this wasn't a line, it was a sentence with two lines, in fact, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thank you again for your assistance in clarifying up a major problem. I thought I just indicated to you whether you would make any distinction between important things and unimportant things. Ms. Pilipovic, that's the letter you're referring to. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's no change to the schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no change. What's the change?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Simply that there was an addition to the exhibit for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So just the exhibits. I indicated to you yesterday that the schedules can perfectly function as giving an overview again and again, and if there's any change, that you also see the order. But if you just put in one witness, then of course it's difficult to find out what exactly -- you have to go through the whole. If the letter would have been, "Please find enclosed a corrigendum," it says, "to the schedule and the corresponding exhibits," and it's just a change -- if all the witnesses were there in the order and say, "This new schedule contains a change in the exhibits concerning Witness H," then it's immediately clear that there is no change in the order of calling the witnesses. And this might be a bit confusing, but this is also one of the unimportant issues. So let's proceed. Unless there's anything else to be discussed at this moment, I would like to have Mr. Jusic brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jusic. You can hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, welcome again in this courtroom this morning. Although it might not be necessary, I'd just like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you made yesterday as a witness in the examination by Mr. Mundis, it was -- no, Mr. Ierace, by Mr. Ierace. Now continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I ask the witness be shown Exhibit P3112.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jusic. Yesterday afternoon, you showed us on the map the location of the four skyscrapers from which you believed fire had originated which resulted in a man being shot in your view. Would you please point out again the approximate location of those four skyscrapers.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area around here, there are these four skyscrapers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take a black marker -- I'm sorry, a blue marker and place a circle over the approximate position of those four skyscrapers.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see on the map the intersection where the tram on which you were travelling received a round?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please mark that with a cross.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, just going back to the circle that you placed around -- that you placed in the approximate position of the four skyscrapers, I notice that you have placed a circle around what appears to be three symbols of perhaps buildings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can be -- if I can just say: I know roughly all the buildings in that area that go along the Miljacka River.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P3644. Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, would you please look at the map that you are about to be handed, and would you first of all locate on that map, if you can, the railway station. There's no need to point to it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps that could be placed on the ELMO, the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please point to the railway station. Don't mark it. Do not mark it; just point to it.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on that map, could you indicate the position of the four skyscrapers that you described yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please place a circle around the four skyscrapers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't this the original map? Please, please, please, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you want to have -- this is an exhibit that has already been admitted into evidence, so if you want any marking made on a similar map, you have to provide a new one to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps there's another way of doing it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to -- would you please compare the two maps in relation to the building -- what appear to be building symbols. That is, go back to the map you've already marked, and is this the position that the four building symbols you have just indicated do not appear on your original map?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to the circle that you have placed on map P3112, is there any change that you wish to make to the position of the circle?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'd that ask, with the assistance of the usher, P3112 be placed back on the ELMO and the other map be removed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, I think you were in the process of placing a cross at the intersection where the tram on which you were travelling was shot. Have you placed that cross on the map? Please place a cross on the map at the appropriate place, if you can see it.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said yesterday in your evidence that, from your observations, there was -- there were two areas which were occupied at the relevant time by the Serb forces, Serb armed forces. One of those you identified as the Jewish cemetery. Can you locate on that map the Jewish cemetery, and if so, could you point to it.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you place a blue circle around the Jewish cemetery, and place, alongside the circle, number "1." First of all, place a circle around the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the cemetery itself?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then alongside it, place a "1."

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Might that be returned. Mr. President, at this stage I ask that the relevant video be shown. It is Exhibit P3279.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if you wouldn't mind, I'd like to clarify the issue you just raised before we continue. Would it be possible, Mr. Usher -- could you please put back on the ELMO the big black-and-white map. Mr. Jusic, you were asked by Mr. Ierace to point also on this map the skyscrapers. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please look at the map and indicate again the skyscrapers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see you pointing at four relatively small rectangular shapes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the left of these rectangular shapes, I find two bigger shapes which are irregular of form; at least, they're not the same, and they are bigger. Do you see them? Could you please point at what I just indicated, these bigger shapes. Could you point at these, so in order to be sure that you understand exactly --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that one, and to the left, a bit north.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are the four smaller rectangular shapes the skyscrapers you referred to, or are the bigger shapes on the map the skyscrapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The four rectangular shapes indicate -- I believe that they indicate that in that area, that those four skyscrapers are indicated on the map as four rectangular shapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But if it is necessary, I do know this area, and I know the entire area from the bridge, from this bridge, from the bridge of Brotherhood and Unity to the bridge which is Suade Kilberovic Street, or bridge, who was a student of medicine who was killed in the beginning of the war, from Dubrovnik, and this is the name of the bridge. And if you want, I can show you exactly what the buildings are in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you know the area well. Could you please look at the other map again, 3112. And put it on the ELMO just beneath the four skyscrapers. I would like to have them both on the ELMO. If Mr. Usher would put the relevant part, so you have to fold the second map. If you would please give it to me, I'll fold it exactly at the spot I would like to have it folded. A bit lower, Mr. Usher. Yes, that way. Mr. Jusic, do you see now on the two maps approximately the same area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you see the four rectangular smaller shapes which you just referred to as being the skyscrapers, also on the lower map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you see the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question quite clear to you. The lower part of the map indicates the same area as the upper map. Do you agree with me that on the upper map there are more shapes than on the lower map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. It is more accurate. The upper map is more accurate. And in addition to the four skyscrapers, these three points here, they are skyscrapers, too. These three are skyscrapers, too, about the same size as the other four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, would you please look at your marking on the lower map. The circle you've drawn, does it with precision indicate the position of the skyscrapers, or could it be slightly different from the irregular forms you have circled around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This irregular shape here is a low structure, and that is the kindergarten. And next to it was the youth centre. It was called Bosko Buha at the time. And then here are -- this here, after -- these four skyscrapers are here, so I need to correct the circle that I made. This is where they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do see on the map, just for the sake of the record, that you make a new circle a bit to the right of the original circle you've drawn. Thank you very much, Mr. Jusic. The maps can be returned to the Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might we see now the video which is P3280, that is, the relevant portion. [Videotape played]: "INVESTIGATOR: Would you please show me by standing at the spot where, to the best of your recollection, the front of the tram was located at the time the tram was hit while you were riding upon it. I will now mark the spot using yellow spray paint. Could you now please show me where approximately, to the best of your recollection, the bullet hit the side of the tram. I will now mark this spot in the figure "X" with a "1" beside it. Would you now please show me where in the tram, to the best of your recollection, you were seated and the direction you were facing when the bullet hit the tram.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was standing, not sitting. INVESTIGATOR: I will mark this spot with an "X" and a number "2" beside it. Could you please show me where, to the best of your recollection, the woman and her four-year-old son were seated in relation to you. I will mark this spot with an "X" and a number "3" beside it. Could you please show me where the other young woman named Belma was located when the bullet hit the tram, to the best of your recollection. I will mark this spot with an "X" with a number "4" beside it. Finally, would you please tell me where, to the best of your recollection, the back of the tram was located. I will mark this line with just a line."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, did you recognise yourself in that video?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you comply with the directions of the investigator truthfully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question. What do you mean by asking me whether I complied with the directions truthfully and to the best?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the video, we observed that the investigator asked you to point out certain things.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understood what the investigator wanted me to do, to show.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you pointed out those things, did you do so to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you do so truthfully?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would now like the Trial Chamber to view Exhibit P3279I. Before it is shown, I should point out that you will note the yellow markings do not appear in those photographs. In due course, there will be evidence to explain that. The photographs were taken three days later; and as luck would have it, during those three days, the road surface was resurfaced. It was also not possible for the tripod to be mounted approximately at the point that this witness indicated the bullet entered the tram. Because of traffic conditions, the tripod was mounted approximately 5 metres further north of that approximate position. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, once we have received the -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think this is a matter of major importance. The Defence still has the same type of objections, all the more so today, because evidently we cannot orient ourselves well in the space. And I also know that there is another problem; I will now verify it. That is the content of the tape was given -- was in the transcript, but I did not hear the witness say yesterday - but perhaps I am wrong - I do not remember him saying that the child who was with his mother was a four-year-old child. But I will check this, and I think that the question which was asked by the investigator on this site made reference to it. But this is a technical problem, and I will check it. Therefore, the Defence objects to the production of this piece of evidence, and we want -- because of what the witness said, I believe, was that the child was two or three years old. In the question, the investigator asked him about the existence of a child of four years. We were not there, so one cannot be objective. This is another technical problem, and I think it is of major importance. Yes, it is a detail, and if I disturbed the Chamber for nothing, then I apologise in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, what's your recollection about as far as the age of the -- I could just look at the transcript, since the wording of the -- used by the investigator are usually also in the transcript. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the relevant part of the transcript on the LiveNote version for yesterday, in English, is page 66, line 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Question: "Approximately how old was the child, if you are able to recollect that?" Answer: "It was a very small child; two, three years of age."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now let's see what the investigator has asked on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's page 13, line 8, Mr. President, and indeed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. Yes. Mr. Jusic, the investigator on the video asks you about the place where a four-year-old child was. Yesterday you testified that the child in the tram you referred to was a very young child, you said two or three years old. While answering the question of the investigator, did you refer, on a question about a four-year-old child, to the same child you indicated yesterday as a young child, two or three years old?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I meant that same child.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is there anything else at this moment? No. Then please -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. I was just going to say that there was nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, do you recognise the image which appears on the screen at the moment, which is of a church at an intersection?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What intersection is that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the intersection of the street formerly called Trscanska and now Fra Andjela Zvizdovica, and the street which the tram was taking, and that was the street of Marsal Tito. Now, this whole street used to be Marsal Tito once. Now, whether it is still called that, I wouldn't know. I do not know. But this is the high street, the main street, and that is Marsal Tito Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please pan the image slowly to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, this is also a moment where I would like to make a remark for all parties. Since there has been manipulation of this 360-degree photograph at a certain moment, without a specific order, you'll notice that those technicians who are manipulating the pictures are now in the courtroom, so that we are in better control. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, so there be no misunderstanding, the person operating the image at the moment is indeed Zoran Lesic, who is the witness I'll be calling next week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we see now another view of Marsal Tito?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is the camera -- having regard to your earlier evidence that the street runs east-west, is the camera facing east or west, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The camera is facing east.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue panning the image to the right. Please pause.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to your earlier evidence, is the camera now facing approximately south?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see on the image the area of the Jewish cemetery, having regard to your earlier evidence?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you see a ridge beyond the mid-ground and, in front of the ridge, two trees with foliage?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have a rather hazy image here. Do you mean the slopes here or do you mean these trees in front, at the intersection itself? I didn't quite understand what trees you meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question. Was the Jewish cemetery somewhere on the relatively flat part of the picture or on the ridge part?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Jewish cemetery is on a slightly elevated ground, right above the transfers, a transfers road which goes through that part of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Towards the centre of the image at the moment, there appears to be a street heading south and some vehicles on that street. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the right of the street is a tree; to the left of the street is a taller tree. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the Jewish cemetery appear between the two trees, or somewhere else, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between those two trees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you also referred to Mount Trebevic. Do you see Mount Trebevic in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see a part of it. Yes, you can see part of Trebevic slopes, but I think this is the area already towards the restaurant called Osmice. But this picture again is rather hazy. Prior to the -- yes, but yes, you can see the slopes of Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interfere at this very moment. What button is pushed for the witness? Since I noted that if you push the video button, I get a picture which is far worse than when I push the Computer Evidence button. Could you, Mr. Usher, please check that the witness has the best image in front of him, by just going through the ... It is the Computer Evidence button which gives the best ... But it might be different. Does the witness have the best image now in front of him? Is this a better image, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is. It is. Yes, it is much clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you now see Mount Trebevic or part of Mount Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see a large part of Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that there is a light pole to the left of centre of the image? The light pole appears to be located in the middle of Marsal Tito Boulevard.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that immediately behind the light pole there appears to be a peak on the ridge line?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us where Mount Trebevic is in relation to that peak?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean by that behind the light pole?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it, in fact, the ridge behind the light pole?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mount behind the lamp pole, you can see the outline, the skyline of the Trebevic ridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the image to the right. Pause there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the name of the building, that is, the high-rise building which appears on the screen at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building used to belong -- at the time of the common state, it was the building of the Government of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the image. Pause there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we now looking west along Marsal Tito Boulevard, having regard to your earlier evidence?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the image to the right. Pause.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the identity of the yellow building, that is, the yellow squarish -- or at least, yellow building of approximately ten storeys.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Holiday Inn Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the image to the right. Please pause and pan back, if you can, or upwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the identity of the brownish high-rise building which appears towards the centre of the image?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the UNIS office building. It was a large company. So this is a skyscraper of the once large company called UNIS, U-N-I-S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the image to the right. All right. And I think we've now completed the circumnavigation of the site. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you please have it turned still a bit more to the right so we can again have a look at the Marsal Tito. Yes, thank you. That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness now be shown the map which is P3112, and also the photographs which are P32795. Excuse me. Yes, I'm sorry, 3279J.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, first of all, look at the map. And in particular, where you have marked the Jewish cemetery, may that be placed on the ELMO. Please point to the Jewish cemetery with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in front of the Jewish cemetery, on the map, there appears to be a road running roughly east-west, crossing all of the part of the map which appears on the video. Do you know the name of that road? I'll withdraw that. First of all, could you point to the road that I've just described.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know the name of that road?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is -- well, we call it a detour road. It was built -- well, there used to be a narrow track, train. The Cheetah used to go along the Trebevic slope. But when this was discontinued, the road was built. It, in fact, carries freight from Pale to take it out of the town, and this freight train moved along those tracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it sometimes also known as the Transit Road?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is known as the Transit Road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please look at photograph P3279J. Perhaps that could be marked on the ELMO, in particular the one marked 22A. Earlier you pointed out the government building on the 360 photograph. Do you see that building on the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please point to it.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also pointed out the UNIS building. Please point to that if you see it on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Holiday Inn, please point to that.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Immediately to the right of the UNIS building, do you see part of a road? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise the road that appears in the foreground of the photograph, that is, the road that runs across the front of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a Transit Road. And you used the same term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please look at the second photograph. And by comparing the two photographs, do you agree that the second photograph appears to be a telephoto shot of the middle portion of the first photograph, that is, the area just to the right of the UNIS building?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see in that photograph, to the right there is a church?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this, indeed, a photograph of the same intersection in which the tram in which you were travelling was shot?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this photograph, and indeed in the intersection, there appears to be a yellow tram. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How does that tram compare to the one in which you were travelling at that time?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is the same direction. It went in the same direction and the same place where the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Mr. President, that completes examination-in-chief, and I apologise for taking so long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I put one question to you before giving an opportunity to the Defence to cross-examine the witness. Mr. Jusic, if I compare the two photographs of which you said that the second one appears to be a telephoto shot of the middle portion of the first photograph, do you mean that it's just taken from the first photograph, or that it is a new shot of the same spot with different lenses?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The latter, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your clarification. Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to whom do I give the opportunity to cross-examine the witness? To you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Jusic, you'll be questioned now by Ms. Pilipovic, who is Defence counsel. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jusic, good morning. Mr. Jusic, yesterday in response to a question by my colleague about what your occupation was in early 1992, you said you were employed in Sipad.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be more precise. When you said it was in early 1992, until when in 1992 were you employed in Sipad?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in Sipad -- well, I am still employed in Sipad Import/Export, but I have been, in fact, hired at the moment to work for the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. My employment in Sipad, in fact, never ceased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, since you said your occupation started in early 1992, were you employed in Sipad? Did you go to work?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was employed for some time, and I used to go to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you used to go to work there. Can you tell us: In 1992, which period was it that you went to work?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, until the end of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: In which part of the town was your place of employment located?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the town centre, in Marsal Tito Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So until June 1992, you used to go to work there?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: In 1992, you said that you were working for Sipad until June. Where, and in which part of the town did you live?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived in the part of the city called Pofalici, in an apartment across the Bristol Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why, for what reason did you stop going to work in the month of June? As far as I understood, you went to work until June.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer why did you stop going to work?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of June, I was employed, engaged in the forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which were there to defend the city, for reasons of self-defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in June 1992, if I understood you well, you joined the armed forces of the B and H army.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't like to speak of when the army of the B and H was formed. I don't think that it was called like that at the time. I had an accreditation card where it was said "Territorial Defence."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said you had an accreditation of the Territorial Defence, can you explain this in greater detail? What did that imply, and how was this, in fact -- how did this look in practice?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had a card with my photo on it, with my name, surname, and the units, the formation, the organisational form, the military organisational form to which I -- where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: What was your organisational form? To which organisational form did you belong? What did it state on your card?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really remember whether it said "organisational form." I don't think that on those first cards, they didn't have this mentioned; just the name, surname, and some personal information, date of birth, and so on. But I don't think that the organisational form was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in what part of the town was your Territorial Defence command post?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local centre, Vaso Miskin Crni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that local centre, Vaso Miskin Crni, what municipality of Sarajevo was it?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Novo Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in what street was your command post in the Vaso Miskin local centre?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the street -- of course, it's called differently today. It was called the Blood Donor Street. Today it is called the Kolodvorska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about your command post in the Blood Donor Street and now the Kolodvorska Street? In what sort of building was that place accommodated, your post accommodated?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was simply a place where we assembled, where we got together, but at the time we had practically no weapons at all. It wasn't a genuine military formation in the true sense of the word and what this implies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in what capacity were you in the Territorial Defence unit? What assignments did you have?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, there was a questionnaire circulated about who would be prepared to help in procuring first aid in the case of war. Well, war hadn't broken out, but we were just preparing. And I attended a first-aid course, providing the wounded with first aid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: Since you have explained what your role was then, were you aware that in 1992 until -- that a call-up had been -- that a recruitment, in fact, mobilisation, was started?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. I think it was publicly announced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can I refresh your memory? Was this in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think it was that early. We can speak of mobilisation only following August, after August 1992, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you were not aware of the fact that in 1992, that mobilisation had been called, in April?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since we are discussing the part of 1992 when you joined the army of B and H, and in June you said what your duties were, can we then accept -- and you have already told our learned colleague that until January 1994 you were a member of the B and H army. Can we accept that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether, during that period, until January 1994, was the B and H army constituted, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question. I don't know the date when this happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period while you were a member of the B and H army, until January 1st, 1994, what was your duty during that period? What sort of military schedule did you follow?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, later I was in the 102nd Motorised Brigade, which was located in the part of town called Stup Azici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as a member of the 102nd Motorised Brigade, you were in the section of the town which was under the control of the B and H army, which is the area of Stup and its surroundings?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: In the part of the city which was under the control of the 102nd Motorised Brigade, where was your command post?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity of Stup. In Stup itself, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: In what building was your command post? Where was your command post located? In which building?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were some buildings there. There used to be a warehouse, the Sava Kranj warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when the 102nd Motorised Brigade was formed, did you receive a uniform then, and what was your assignment at that time?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any uniform. I didn't have any special assignment except the first aid course activities. And at the time, I had a rifle and 50 -- an M-48 and 15 bullets in my pocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, when you became a member of the 102nd Motorised Brigade, did you receive armaments, the M-48 rifle, can you tell us, did you have any special identification card when you were assigned to that task?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was given a new card at the time, where it said "Army," "B and H army." I cannot recall exactly the appearance of the card and what it contained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as a member of the 102nd Motorised Brigade, you had an M-48 rifle and you didn't have a uniform. Can you tell us how many people belonged to the 102nd Motorised Brigade? How many people were in that formation?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many smaller formations there were within the brigade, specifically, how many battalions and how many companies?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have that information. Even at the time, we weren't fully organised according to usual military rules. I know something about this because I had served the former Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the commander of the 102nd Motorised Brigade was, whether it was a trained officer or --

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was a trained officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the officers personnel of the army, B and H army, and of the 1st Corps, which was on the territory of the city of Sarajevo, that the commanders were, in fact, former commanders of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them were, but I don't know exactly, of all the superior staff there, who had had experience or ranks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in that particular part of the town where the 102nd Motorised Brigade was located, which part of the town did you cover? Where were the front lines, more specifically, in that part of the town?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the front lines changed from 1992 until mid-1993 [as interpreted]. The B and H army forces were being [Realtime transcript read in error "expressed"] suppressed at the time, and we had been losing some of the front lines. The first front lines were in Otes, in Livade, in Azici. And subsequently, the lines were drawn up to the very location of Stup.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President; two matters in relation to the transcript. I note that they don't have the symbol that indicates they may be reviewed later. The first is page 30, line 3. It reads: "The front lines changed from 1992 until mid-1993." The translator, I think I heard her say "until May 1993." Perhaps that could be clarified. Secondly, same page, line 4 reads: "The B and H army forces were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. being expressed at the time." The translation I heard was "forces were suppressed at the time." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I expect proper care will be taken to those remarks, Mr. Ierace. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you have just answered the question about the front lines, if the Defence were to show you a town plan of Sarajevo covering that particular section, could you draw in to the map, into that part of the map where the front lines were, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that Stup -- well, on the more restricted part, I would be able to do this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Court pleases, we have town plan which reflects Stup. We would like to show the witness the map and have him mark where the positions were in that section of the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... it's the first time that we have used this map, or is it the big black-and-white or... ?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is the town plan of Sarajevo. And during the earlier testimonies -- testimonies, my colleagues used parts of it. And I copied this to make things easier, more simple. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I think that would get Number 336, because it's another part of the map that has been used before, so far as I understand. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'll get the number. D37.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 37. Yes, there was a mistake. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, please take a black marker and indicate on that part of the map where the command post was located and where the front lines were located.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Command post was somewhere here, about somewhere -- yes, about somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you --

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm not quite sure. It was a place where the command personnel was, in fact, accommodated. I don't know it was a command post or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please draw that circle and write Number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it would be a good moment, Your Honour, to break now because it is time for a pause, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you'll start with the circle after the break, because I do not see a circle yet on the screen. So do you want the witness to mark it now or to start with it?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let him draw the circle now and write number "1."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, where you have drawn the cross...

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then adjourn until 11.00. Mr. Jusic, we'll see you then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, Zoran Lesic has now been replaced by Drazen Vitolovic from the video unit to operate the 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I was just informed by the registry that the limited space in the public gallery in this courtroom could be an obstacle for people who want to attend, to attend this courtroom live instead of on television. I gave the order that when there's still space for a person in the public gallery, and if there is not enough chairs, rather than keeping someone out of the public gallery and provide the chairs somewhere else, rather a chair would be brought in so that the public character of this trial is as much warranted as possible. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. What I wanted to say, that - this is about today in particular - we are very grateful for your remark. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was informed only a few seconds ago about the specific aspects of the public character of this trial today, and this was the decision I took. Then I think, Mr. Ierace, we could -- oh, yes. I'm afraid that -- no, I'm -- I apologise for not being very attentive. Ms. Pilipovic, you may proceed with the cross-examination of Mr. Jusic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before the break you indicated and marked for us on the map that's before you the location which was the command post of the 102nd Motorised Brigade. As far as you can recall, could you mark for us on this map the front lines in this area of the city.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can just say: I am not sure whether this was the command post, but this was -- I'm not quite sure whether this was exactly the command post, but if we're talking about the front line, I can say that the last, the last lines, the last front lines, in mid-1993 until about May 1993. That's what I can indicate. Or do you want me to indicate the lines that I found, as it were, when I came to Stup?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to mark the lines that you found when you came to Stup.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lines, when I arrived at Stup in October 1992, were about here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you don't mind, could you please take the black marker and make a marking where the front line went.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time -- I can only do it approximately, as far as I know where the line went, where I was. So it was about here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So this is the front line where you were. Could you tell us: In that area where you were, at which distance or how far was the front line of the other side? What was -- how far away was the other line? How far were the two lines apart?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About where the fields are, I presume that this was a rather deep line. I'm not quite sure how far. Here, where the houses were, the line was a little shorter, perhaps in some places as short as 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now you told us about the front line where you were, and you indicated the demarcation line, the confrontation line. And yesterday we agreed that this was the line between the BH army and the Republika Srpska army, that the demarcation line was about 100 metres in one part of the line.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In one part of the line where there were houses, there were residential buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us, how long did you spend at the front line? When I'm talking about how long, I mean during the day, during the week. Was it days or weeks?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at the beginning of -- in early October, when I arrived at Stup, we found lines that were practically empty. I presume that the arrival of our unit, which wasn't prepared in any particular way -- we were not prepared for any kind of combat action. We just arrived at this kind of empty area. And if I remember well, this was the time when the BH army had also some units and some parts of units that were led by Juka Prazina. So there were some problems, and then they withdrew from these lines. They were no longer there. And after I arrived, about two or three days later, there was a fierce attack of the Serb forces in that period. And at that time, I was seriously injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. But I would like to just have your answer as to how long -- how much time you spent there.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent there two or three days, and that's when I was seriously injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those two days that you were at the front for three days [as interpreted], where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We slept in the cellars of the existing residential objects, residential buildings. If there were no cellars, then we were just on the ground floor of these houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the front line to go home, did you have organised transport as members of that unit, the transport to your house, to your home?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We went individually. We went on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you just mentioned Juka Prazina, problems related -- conflicts related to Juka Prazina's unit, could you tell us whether these units had any specific particular insignia that differentiated them from you as members of the territorial defence and later as members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was I did not find any soldiers there. I said I heard that they were there before. I never saw members of those units except in some, in some -- in some particular items that were in the media or on television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw them on television, did you have any specific insignia [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had some kind of uniforms. I don't know whether you can call that a uniform. But yes, yes, I suppose they had a kind of -- uniform of sorts. Some of them, I'm not quite sure how many there were of them, but some of them had -- some of them had distinguishing uniforms. I don't know whether they were all dressed like that. I'm not sure. I was never in contact with those units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, let us return to the location of the incident when you were in the tram in June 1994. Could you be accurate and tell us exactly which day in June that happened?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an accurate answer to that. The actual date, I cannot tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that, after being asked by my learned colleague, that the tram was shot at the moment when it was at the intersection of the Marsal Tito Street and Trscanska Street. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether in the vicinity of that place there is a tram stop, although we saw the tram was at the intersection?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The stop coming from the direction of the town is further away from the place of the incident, and the following is a little bit lower, a little below. So no, there is no tram stop in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- you told us that you got on the tram near the presidency building?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were then working there. Could you tell us whether that building, whether that building, while you were working there, your workplace, was there security provided for that building?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether in that building there were military personnel, in that building?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what is the following stop after the presidency building where you got on the tram?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any building -- specific building where the next stop is?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following stop is Marin Dvor. And apart from the buildings that we saw on the actual video, the stop is a little further away, a little more towards the east. There are no characteristic buildings, specific buildings. These are just buildings from the Austria-Hungarian era.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that part where the tram line goes, we have the Holiday Inn building. Is that correct? We saw that building?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The UNIS building?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the presidency building of the Presidency of BH?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the stop after Marin Dvor, is that the Holiday Inn stop?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you allow for the possibility that the tram at the moment when it was shot at, that it was actually at the stop in front of the Holiday Inn Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, the interpreters could not hear your last answer. I think the question was about whether the tram was at the tram stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was: Would the following stop after the Marin Dvor stop is in front of the Holiday Inn Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stop is not right in front. It is a stop which comes from the direction of Ilidza, from the westward direction. But it doesn't stop directly in front of Holiday Inn, but a little bit further, a little bit to the west. But the stop that comes from the town is also not quite in front of the hotel, but it's some 50 metres away to the west as we go out of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say west going out of the town, is that a stop which is practically -- if we say that we're going towards the street Zmaja Od Bosne or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my friend, in fact, misunderstands the question to which an answer was not recorded. The question appears at page 38, line 11 and reads: Would you allow for the possibility that the tram at the moment when it was shot at, that it was actually at the stop in front of the Holiday Inn Hotel? That's the question that requires an answer. For my own part, I did hear an answer, but perhaps the witness could be asked to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please, because that was the question asked at that very moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think the witness said no, but the witness could answer again.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm my previous answer that the tram was not on the stop in front of the Holiday Inn. So it's no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, perhaps we could first instruct the witness. Mr. Jusic, since you are speaking both the same language, sometimes questions and answers come so quickly that the interpreters have difficulties in following it. If you would please look at the screen in front of you, and perhaps wait until the text stops moving, and then answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to apologise. You're not aware of the problem, perhaps. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I can -- if you'll allow me, now I'm checking the transcript, and the witness actually answered the question saying, "The stop is not right in front," which can be seen on line 21, 11.13. And I believe that he answered with all clarity required. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's my recollection that the witness answered the question, that it was common understanding what his answer was. And that answering one of the questions that were put to him later on, that this answer might be understood as a precision of what he testified before. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that at the moment when, according to you, the tram was targeted, you were wounded, a young woman who was standing next to you, and a woman with a child that you described yesterday as being two or three years of age. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again, my friend is not putting to the witness what the evidence was. In particular, my friend has put to the witness that his evidence was that a young woman was standing next to him. In fact, my recollection is that the witness said that the woman was standing about a metre away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is the distance between the witness and the young woman of any relevance for your later questioning?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that there's no misunderstanding. It's not very precise, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence just wanted to identify the persons that the witness saw at the moment they were in the tram, when, according to the witness, the tram was shot. So my question was asked because the Defence would like to have the witness shown a statement that the Defence was given by the Prosecution, and this is the statement by a witness who was in the tram when the shooting occurred. And this statement -- the Defence has this statement in English and in B/C/S. Now, what I would like to show the witness is the part of the witness statement about where the incident happened. Now, if I'm looking at the statement of this witness, written statement of this witness, the female witness and this witness that we're hearing today, there is a difference in the description of the location in the Marsal Tito Street about where the incident happened. Your Honour, this is the statement by Belma Likic. This is the young woman who was standing nearby the witness on the day in question when the incident happened. And with your permission, this is the Belma Likic statement, Prosecution document, page 2, 00360838. Now, the Defence would like to show the witness this statement, the part of the statement which is just about one line, paragraph 3 of the statement, and we would like to ask the witness about this so that we can be precise about the location of the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's just about one line, could you please read, then, that line and indicate to Mr. Jusic that you are reading -- I'm already indicating it to him at this moment. Ms. Pilipovic will be reading one line of a statement. But, Mr. Ierace, I see you're standing on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we weren't given any forewarning that my friend was going to do this. I think my friend said she has an English copy of the statement. Perhaps she could make that available to us while she reads the line. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please ... Ms. Pilipovic, are you -- you're going to read it in the original language, I think at least the original language of the person who gave --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It could just be given, for information purposes, to the -- please give it to Mr. Ierace. Mr. Jusic, Ms. Pilipovic will now read a very limited portion of a statement given by someone else on the same incident. Would you please listen carefully to this line read by Ms. Pilipovic but which is a portion of a statement of another person. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is a portion of a statement given by a girl who was in the tram together with you. This is paragraph 3 of this statement. It begins with the words, "The incident..." "The incident happened in front of the Holiday Inn Hotel, at the intersection with the street Franje Rackog Street." Witness, would you allow for the possibility that the incident happened in front of the Holiday Inn Hotel, at the intersection with the Franje Rackog Street and Marsal Tito Street, or the incident happened at the intersection of the Trscanska Street and the Marsal Tito Street, which is what you told us today?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am absolutely certain in the statement that I gave, and I think I can support this by the following: The tram, in its continued movement, had to cross the street which is parallel to it, going to the left, and I remember very well that all of us who were present and had fallen on the floor of the tram, all of us who were there -- because this is a very sharp manoeuvre that the tram has to perform, and we -- it was very hard for the tram to turn. So it was a lady who was a tram driver, and the tram continued moving. So it cannot be that the incident happened after this, at the following intersection. I'm absolutely certain of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, you told us a moment ago that at the moment when you heard the shot, the tram gained speed and turned right. Can you tell us what street was it that the tram took when it turned right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the -- my friend might put to the witness precisely what he said in that regard. I don't have any recollection of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you -- could you please give us the -- yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at the moment of the incident, when the tram -- as you said, you went down to the ground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you said the tram accelerated.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the tram went on moving. [Realtime transcript read in error: "Q. And then you said the tram accelerated. Well, the tram went on moving."]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: In which direction did the tram continue to move?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said earlier that the tram was to cross the street which runs parallel with the tram tracks to the left. You asked me about the right turn, but I spoke about the left turn, and you can see it well on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. And this turn that you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interfere, just for the sake of the record. At 11:30:13, which is page 44, line 14, after the first sentence, which reads: "And then you said the tram accelerated." It continues: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. "Well, the tram went on moving." It's my recollection that it was the witness who said: "Well, the tram went on moving." And then your question, Ms. Pilipovic, continues: "Can you tell us: In which direction did the tram continue to move?" So the middle part of these two and a half lines was spoken by the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
